title: Same chance, new choice (2:1)
hook: complete return: meeting the same situation, able to do it again, and choosing not to
tomorrow: so what are the steps before the chance comes back?

segments.voice: Look at this week. We will return to you. From time to peace. Finished and begun. You finished a tractate. Ten chapters on returning. And yesterday: say it out loud. A book closed with the hadran's promise, and a new one opened with an apology.
screen: `SIX LINES THIS WEEK.` → `SAY IT OUT LOUD.` → `A PROMISE, THEN AN APOLOGY.`

segments.voice: Same group chat. Same person posting the same thing that set you off last time. Your thumbs already know the reply. You said sorry for that reply, and meant it. So how would you ever know you've really changed? Maimonides says you find out right here. Not in the apology. In the moment the old chance comes back, exactly the same, and you could do it again.
screen: `SAME CHAT. SAME BAIT.` → `HOW WOULD YOU KNOW?` → `WHEN THE CHANCE COMES BACK.`

segments.voice: Here's chapter two, the first law, in plain words. What is complete return? When the chance to do the same wrong comes to a person again, and they're able to do it, and they hold back, because they've returned. Not out of fear, and not because they've grown too weak. Maimonides makes it vivid: the same person, the same place, the same strength, the same pull. Everything lined up like before. And this time, a different choice. Then he adds something kind. If someone only returns late, when they can no longer do the old thing anyway, it still counts. They're still one who has returned, even if it isn't called complete. So the apology is real, and so is the late return. But the proof lives in a moment you can't schedule. Something to tell a friend tonight: in this law, the test of change isn't avoiding the old situation. It's meeting it, fully able, and choosing new.
screen: `THE SAME CHANCE COMES BACK.` · `ABLE, AND HOLDING BACK.` · `A LATE RETURN STILL COUNTS.` · then, large: `SAME CHANCE, NEW CHOICE.`

segments.voice: Sit with your hands open on your knees. Picture where an old habit of yours usually shows up: the place, the person, the hour. See yourself there, fully able to do the old thing, and let your open hands choose something else.
screen: `HANDS OPEN.` · `THE PLACE. THE PERSON. THE HOUR.` · `ABLE, AND CHOOSING NEW.`

segments.voice: Same chance. Maimonides' test of complete return: the old situation, the old strength, and a new choice.
Pocket line: same chance, new choice, and the moment you can't schedule. Three of thirty.

screen: `DAY 1540 COUNTS.` → `THE LAWS OF RETURN · 3 OF 30.` → `TOMORROW: SO WHAT ARE THE STEPS BEFORE THE CHANCE COMES BACK?`
